assemblies.name: Front bumper assembly

signs.ask: Is the bumper cover pushed inward, not just scratched or cracked?
Does a bumper end hang low or stand away from the fender?
Is a bumper-to-lamp or bumper-to-fender gap closed or uneven?
Is the grille, or the opening above the bumper, pushed in?
Is coolant or another fluid on the ground under the front?
Is the bumper's lower edge torn, or plastic hanging under the front?

assemblies.notes: Weakest first: cover and clips, then brackets and absorber, then the beam, then crash boxes and rails. A scuffed cover alone means nothing deeper.

signs.ask: Is the grille pushed in, not just scratched or missing a slat?
Can you see bent cooling fins or pipes through the grille?
Is the bonnet's front edge just above the grille dented or lifted?

assemblies.name: Front end: radiator support and cooling
assemblies.notes: Hidden parts behind the bumper and grille, reached from the front bumper, grille, bonnet and headlamps; never walked from a photo of their own.

signs.ask: Is the bonnet open, tied down, or not closed flush at the front?
Is the gap from the bonnet to a fender uneven at a rear corner?
Is the bonnet folded or creased right across, not just dented?
Is the bonnet's front edge pushed back or bent down?
Is the lamp loose, tilted, or out of line with the other lamp?
Is the bumper corner below the lamp pushed in or torn?
Are the lamp's housing edges or mounting tabs broken, not only the lens?
Is the arch liner inside the fender torn, pushed in or hanging?
Is the front wheel set back or turned, against the other side?
Is the fender pushed back so far that its gap to the door has closed?
Is the fender's front end, beside the headlamp, pushed in or torn?

assemblies.name: Front windscreen

signs.ask: Is the screen holed or pushed into the cabin, not just cracked?
Through the glass, is the dashboard top pushed, torn or covered in glass?

assemblies.notes: Moulding, cowl, wipers, camera and rain sensor go with the screen but have no part name yet.

signs.ask: Is the door pushed in deeply in its lower half, or its skin torn?
Does the door look jammed, not closed flush, or tied shut?
Does the door sag, or have an uneven gap at its front or rear edge?
Is the door glass broken, stuck part way, or out of its run?
In a cabin photo, is the door card pushed in or a side airbag out?
Does the dent reach the door's bottom edge and the sill below it?

assemblies.name: Rear door (each side)

signs.ask: Is the door pushed in deeply in its lower half, or its skin torn?
Does the door look jammed, not closed flush, or tied shut?
Does the door sag, or have an uneven gap at its front or rear edge?
Is the door glass broken, stuck part way, or out of its run?
In a cabin photo, is the door card pushed in or a side airbag out?
Does the dent reach the door's bottom edge and the sill below it?

assemblies.notes: Sliding rear doors (many MPVs) run on rails and rollers, not hinges: the hinge suggestion does not apply there. Two-door cars have no rear door.

assemblies.name: Sill / rocker (each side)

signs.ask: Is the sill pushed inward so the door's bottom gap has closed?
Is the centre pillar above the sill bent, or its gap to the doors changed?

assemblies.notes: Inner sill, centre pillar, floor pan and crossmember sit behind the sill; today only Underbody / Chassis names them.

signs.ask: Is the roof pushed down at its front edge, above the windscreen?
Is the roof pushed down at its rear edge, above the rear glass?
Is the roof pushed down so far that the door tops or pillars look bent?

assemblies.name: Airbags and restraints

signs.ask: Has a bag come out of the dashboard on the passenger side?
Has a bag come out of the outer side of a seat?
Is a curtain bag hanging down from the roof edge above the doors?

assemblies.notes: A fired bag is listed as Airbag System; belt pretensioners, sensors, the clock spring and the SRS unit go with it but have no part name yet.

assemblies.name: Rear bumper assembly

signs.ask: Is the bumper cover pushed inward, not just scratched or cracked?
Does a bumper end hang low or stand away from the body?
Is the gap from the bumper top to the boot lid closed or uneven?
Is a bumper corner pushed in under a tail lamp?
Is the tailpipe pushed in, bent or hanging low?
Boot open: is the floor lifted, or the panel under the opening buckled?

assemblies.notes: Rear Parking Sensor is a member only: the bumper keeps L1's link to Parking Sensor, so the two never show together.

assemblies.name: Boot lid / tailgate

signs.ask: Is the lid open, tied shut, or not closed flush?
Are the gaps along the lid's top corners or sides uneven?
Is the lid creased or buckled, not just dented?
Is the lid's lower edge pushed in, by the lock or plate?
On a tailgate, is the glass cracked or its frame bent?

assemblies.notes: Boot Lid also means a tailgate. On a tailgate the rear glass, wiper and often the high stop lamp ride on the lid; on a sedan the glass sits in the body.

assemblies.name: Rear end panel

signs.ask: Is the panel under the boot opening buckled, or its sealer cracked?
Is the striker bent, or does the lid fail to latch?
Is the boot floor or the spare wheel well lifted or wrinkled?
Are the boot's inner corner trims cracked or pushed in?

assemblies.notes: A pickup has a bed and a tailgate instead: no end panel, boot floor or boot trims.

signs.ask: Is the boot floor board lifted, bent up or cracked across?
With the board up, is the spare wheel well pushed up or wrinkled?

assemblies.name: Tail lamp (each side)

signs.ask: Is the lamp pushed into the body, not just its lens cracked?
Is the gap round the lamp uneven or closed?
Is the lamp's inner end, by the lid lamp, broken or out of line?

assemblies.notes: Catalogues file all rear lamps together; on the car they sit apart, so sharing a diagram is not a damage link.

signs.ask: Is the quarter wrinkled or pushed in around the tail lamp opening?
Is the arch lip dented, or the arch liner torn or hanging?
Does the rear wheel lean or turn more than the other side?
Has the bumper end below the quarter come loose or out of line?
Is the dent low on the quarter's front, just behind the rear door?
Is the rear wiper arm bent or torn off, or its spindle pushed in?
Is the glass smashed, with the tailgate frame round it bent?

assemblies.name: Engine undercover

signs.ask: Is the undercover torn, cracked through, or pushed up into the car?
Is oil or coolant dripping, or on the ground under the front?
Are there fresh scrapes on the cover's rear part, near the exhaust pipe?
Is a front wheel turned or leaning compared with the other?

assemblies.notes: The oil sump sits right above the cover's middle; it has no part name yet.

assemblies.name: Front subframe, suspension and steering

signs.ask: Is a subframe, arm or crossmember visibly bent, kinked or freshly scraped?
Does a front wheel lean, turn or sit set back compared with the other?
In a cabin photo, is the steering wheel off-centre while the wheels look straight?

assemblies.notes: Arms, knuckle, strut and tie rods are written as Suspension - Front and Steering Assembly today; any of them pulls in a wheel alignment.

assemblies.name: Rear subframe and suspension

signs.ask: Is a rear arm, axle beam or subframe visibly bent or freshly scraped?
Does a rear wheel lean, turn or sit closer to its arch than the other?
Is fuel dripping, or the ground wet, under the rear of the car?
Is the floor above the rear axle pushed up, or the boot floor lifted?

assemblies.notes: Most small front-drive cars have a torsion-beam axle and no rear subframe, hence if fitted.

assemblies.name: Underbody and floor

signs.ask: Are there fresh scrapes or dents along the underside or the sill bottoms?
Is fuel, oil or coolant dripping, or on the ground under the car?
Is a wheel leaning, turned or out of line with the others?
Is the exhaust or an under-tray hanging low or off its mounts?

assemblies.notes: Underbody / Chassis also stands in for the rails, crash boxes and floor crossmembers, which have no part name yet.

signs.ask: Is the rim lip bent, flattened or cracked, not just scraped?
Is the wheel set back or turned, against the other side?
Does the wheel lean in or out at the top?
Is the tyre cut, bulging or flat next to the rim damage?
Is the arch liner behind the wheel torn, or the tyre rubbing on it?
Is the rim lip bent, flattened or cracked, not just scraped?
Is the wheel set back or turned, against the other side?
Does the wheel lean in or out at the top?
Is the tyre cut, bulging or flat next to the rim damage?
Is the arch liner behind the wheel torn, or the tyre rubbing on it?

relations.reason: The grille clips into or beside the bumper cover; a cracked or pushed-in cover often breaks its tabs or mesh.
Plate and holder are fixed to the cover; a dent or crack at the plate usually bends or cracks them.
The lamp bezel or blank cover clips into the bumper's lower corner; a crack or push there snaps it, fog lamp or not.
Fog lamps sit in the bumper cover; a crack or dent next to one can break the lamp or its bracket.
Sensors sit in holes in the cover; a dent or crack near one pushes it in, breaks its holder or cuts its wire.

prior.source: K2 A01: often (H, M, T, C)

relations.reason: The cover's end clips into a side bracket under the headlamp; a torn, sagging or pushed bumper end usually snaps it.

prior.source: K2 A01: often (H, M, R, C)

relations.reason: Sits behind the cover and foam absorber; a pushed-in cover can bend it. Check with the bumper off.
Foam or plastic absorber on the beam's face, behind the cover; it crushes when the cover is pushed in.
The bumper end fixes to the front of the arch liner; a cracked or torn bumper end often tears the liner edge.
The undercover is fixed to the bumper's lower edge; a pushed-in or torn lower bumper can tear it or pull it down.
The bumper corner meets the headlamp; a pushed-in or shifted corner can crack the lamp or snap its hidden mounting tabs.
The first cooling part behind the bumper and grille; a pushed-in front can bend its fins or crack its pipes.
Sits behind the condenser; a deep frontal push can bend its core or crack its tanks. Coolant on the ground is the sign.
The frame round the radiator that holds the latch and lamp mounts; a frontal crush past the beam bends it.
A crumpling frontal hit runs from the beam into the rails and subframe; it needs measuring once parts are off.
The steering rack sits on the front subframe; a crush hit that moves the subframe can bend the rack or tie rods.
A crush hit at a corner can push a front wheel back and bend arms or a strut; a wheel set back or turned is the sign.
A hard frontal hit can fire the front airbags and lock the belt pretensioners; check cabin photos for a deployed bag.
The support sits right behind the beam; a beam bent back far enough to see reaches it and its latch and lamp mounts.
The beam bolts to crash boxes on the front rails; a beam pushed back at its end can kink a box or rail. Measure.
Sits right behind the grille; a grille pushed in, not just scratched, often dents the condenser fins or pipes.
Sits behind the grille and condenser; check it when the grille is pushed in or the bonnet front edge is dented.
The grille sits on or just ahead of the support's upper bar; a grille pushed in deeply can bend that bar and its latch.
The radiator sits just behind the condenser; a condenser pushed back can bend the radiator core or crack a tank.
The condenser sits in front of the radiator and takes the hit first; a damaged radiator nearly always means a hit condenser.
The fan and its shroud sit behind the radiator; a radiator pushed back cracks the shroud or breaks the blades.
The radiator hangs in the support's frame; a radiator pushed back far enough to break usually bends its mounts too.
The bonnet latch bolts to the support's upper bar; a bent support stops the bonnet closing or jams the latch.
The headlamps' inner mounts sit on the support; a bent support cracks their tabs or leaves them out of line.
The radiator is held in the support; a support pushed back carries the radiator with it.
The condenser mounts on the support beside the radiator; a bent support bends or pierces it.
The fan and shroud hang on the support or the radiator behind it; a support pushed back can crack them.
The support's lower bar ties the front rails together; a crushed support can mean the rails behind it are bent.
The pad clipped under the bonnet is renewed when the bonnet is buckled or replaced, on cars that have one.

prior.source: K2 A03: often (T, S, H, C)

relations.reason: The latch on the support holds the bonnet's front edge; a bonnet that will not shut or open, or a pushed-back edge, points at it.

prior.source: K2 A03: often (T, S, H, C)

relations.reason: The hinges sit at the bonnet's rear corners; a bonnet pushed back or folded bends them. Uneven rear corner gaps are the sign.
A bonnet folded back toward the cabin can hit the windscreen base and cowl; look for cracks along the lower edge.
The bonnet's front edge closes onto the support's upper bar; a front edge pushed back or bent down can bend that bar.
A headlamp broken with the bumper corner pushed in means the beam end below it may have taken the load too.
The lamp and the bumper end share a bracket on many cars; a loose or pushed-in lamp often comes with a broken bracket.
The lamp's inner mounts bolt to the support; a lamp pushed in hard, tabs broken, can mean the support behind is bent.
The arch trim clips onto the fender's arch lip; a dent there often cracks it or breaks its clips.
The liner is fixed inside the fender's arch; a dent near the arch often tears it or leaves it hanging.
The fender's front edge holds the headlamp's side; a fender pushed back can crack the lamp or its mounting tabs.
A hit at the front corner can push the wheel back and bend an arm or the strut; a wheel set back or turned is the sign.
A wheel pushed back at the corner can bend the tie rod or rack; a turned wheel or off-centre steering is the sign.
A crush hit at the front corner can move the subframe corner; it needs measuring with parts off.
Behind the fender sit the inner apron and the front rail; a crumpled fender can mean they are bent too.
A screen holed or pushed into the cabin, or burst by a passenger airbag, can damage the dashboard top below it.
The mirror is mounted at the door's front corner; a dent there can crack the housing or loosen the mount.
A door pushed in, or with its frame twisted, can crack the glass or push it out of its run.
The outer handle sits in the door skin; a dent or scrape across it often cracks or scratches it.
The lock sits in the door's rear edge; a door that will not open or latch, or one pushed in at that edge, has a bent lock.
The hinges hold the door's front edge to the pillar; a door that sags, drops when opened or sits out of line has bent hinges.
The regulator sits inside the door; a deep dent in the lower half, a torn skin or stuck glass means it may be bent.

prior.source: K2 A09: sometimes, as door trim card (M, S)

relations.reason: The door trim card on the inside cracks or loses its clips when the door is pushed in.
Load from a door pushed in at the bottom goes into the sill; a crease along the sill below the door is the sign.
A door pushed into the cabin can fire the side or curtain airbag; check cabin photos for a deployed bag.
The glass rides on the regulator inside the door; glass stuck, out of its run or pushed in usually means a bent regulator.
sources: oem: FRONT DOOR GLASS / DOOR REGULATOR

prior.source: K2 A12: rare, as floor crossmember (S)

relations.reason: The sill joins the floor crossmembers; a sill crushed inward can bend the floor and crossmember behind it.
On a tailgate car the high stop lamp sits at the roof's rear edge or its spoiler; a dent there can crack it.

prior.source: K2 A14: sometimes, as headliner (T, S)

relations.reason: The headliner is glued and clipped under the roof; a roof dented in creases or tears it.
The screen is bonded to the roof's front edge; a roof pushed down there often cracks it from the top.
The rear glass is bonded to the roof's rear edge or sits just below it; a roof pushed down there can crack it.
A passenger airbag bursts through the dashboard top; once it has fired, that panel or its bag door is renewed.
A side airbag sits in the seat's outer bolster; once it has fired, the seat cover or frame is renewed.
A curtain airbag tears the headliner edge and pillar trims as it fires; they are renewed with it.
Reflectors sit in the bumper ends; a crack or dent at that corner often breaks the reflector or its clips.
Sensors sit in holes in the cover; a dent or crack near them can push them in, break the holders or cut the wiring.
Plate and holder sit on the bumper or just above it; a dent or crack at the plate usually bends or cracks them.
Where the camera sits in the bumper or the garnish just above it, a bumper pushed up or in can crack or misalign it.
The cover's end clips into a side bracket on the quarter; a torn, sagging or pushed bumper end usually snaps it.
Foam or plastic absorber on the rear beam's face, behind the cover; it crushes when the cover is pushed in.

prior.source: K2 A17: often (T, M, R, C)

relations.reason: Sits behind the cover and absorber; a pushed-in cover or an uneven boot-to-bumper gap can mean it is bent.
The bumper end fixes to the rear arch liner; a cracked or torn bumper end often tears the liner edge.
The panel under the boot opening, behind the bumper; an uneven boot gap or a buckle under the boot sill is the sign.
The bumper corner sits under the tail lamp; a corner pushed up, in or shifted can crack the lens or the housing.
A rear panel pushed forward can lift, bend or crack the boot floor board; it is seen with the boot open.
Boot side trims line the inside of the rear corners; a pushed-in corner can crack them or break their clips.
The tailpipe ends at the bumper; a pushed-in bumper can bend the pipe or break its hangers.
A crush hit runs through the rear rails into the spare wheel well and floor; wrinkles show under the boot carpet.
A crush hit at a rear corner can push the wheel and bend an arm or the axle; a wheel turned or set back is the sign.
The tank sits ahead of the rear floor; a deep rear crush can dent it or its filler pipe. Fuel on the ground is the sign.
The rear beam bolts to crash boxes on the rear rails; a beam pushed in at its end can kink a box or rail. Measure.
Lamps mounted on the lid crack or come loose when the lid is dented or pushed in next to them.
Where the plate sits on the lid, a dent at the lid's centre bends the plate or its holder.
The plate lamp sits above the plate, in the lid or its garnish; a dent there cracks it.
The trim strip across the lid holds the plate lamps and often the camera; a dent across it cracks it or breaks its clips.
On many cars the camera sits in the lid's garnish above the plate; a dent there can crack or misalign it.
A spoiler on the lid's edge cracks or breaks its mounts when the lid is dented or twisted, on cars that have one.
On many cars the high stop lamp sits on the lid's top edge or spoiler; a lid twisted or pushed in can crack it.
On a tailgate or hatch the rear glass sits in the lid, so a twisted lid can crack it. Not on a sedan's boot lid.
The lock sits in the lid's lower edge; a buckled lid, or one that will not open or latch, usually means a bent lock.
The striker the lock catches sits on the panel under the lid; a lid that will not latch, or a buckled lower edge, points at it.
A lid pushed forward or out of line bends its hinges; uneven gaps at the lid's top corners are the sign.
Gas struts hold a tailgate or lid up; a lid pushed out of line bends them. Some lids use springs instead.
The seal round the boot opening is cut or pushed out of place when the lid or the panel under it buckles.
The trim or insulator on the inside of the lid cracks or loses its clips when the lid is buckled or pushed in.
Inside a tailgate under the glass; a tailgate pushed in at its centre can crack the motor or bend its spindle.
The lid closes onto the rear end panel; a lid pushed in, or hitting on closing, often means that panel buckled too.
The boot seal fits on this panel's top flange; a buckled panel cuts it or lifts it off.
The striker bolts to this panel's top edge; a panel pushed forward bends it and the lid then fails to latch.
The floor board rests against this panel inside the boot; a panel pushed forward lifts, bends or cracks it.
The boot side trims meet this panel at the inner corners; a corner pushed in cracks them or breaks their clips.
The lock's striker is on this panel; a panel pushed forward stops the lid latching or jams the lock.
The rear end panel is welded to the boot floor; a panel pushed forward wrinkles the floor and spare wheel well behind it.
sources: oem: OUTER PANELS / REAR PANEL > FLOOR / INNER PANELS (next diagram)

relations.reason: The board covers the spare wheel well; a board lifted or cracked from below often means the floor under it is pushed up.
The lamp sits in an opening in the quarter; a pushed-in lamp can wrinkle that opening, often seen only with the lamp out.

prior.source: K2 A19: sometimes, a neighbour (M, C)

relations.reason: The lid lamp sits right beside the tail lamp; a hit that cracks or pushes in one often reaches the other.
The tail lamp sits in the quarter; a dent at the lamp opening often cracks the lamp or breaks its mounts.
On the side that has the filler, a dent across the flap bends it or its hinge so it no longer shuts flush.
The arch trim clips onto the quarter's arch lip; a dent there often cracks it or breaks its clips.
The liner is fixed inside the quarter's arch; a dent near the arch often tears it or leaves it hanging.
The bumper's end clips into a bracket on the quarter; a dent low at the quarter's rear corner often snaps it.
The boot side trim lines the inside of the quarter; a pushed-in quarter cracks it or breaks its clips.
The quarter's rear end joins the rear end panel; a quarter pushed in at the back can buckle it.
A hit at the rear corner can push the wheel in and bend an arm or the axle; a wheel turned or rubbing is the sign.
sources: oem: OUTER PANELS / REAR PANEL > FLOOR / INNER PANELS (next diagram)

relations.reason: The quarter's lower front edge meets the sill behind the rear door; a low hit there can crease the sill's rear end.
A crumpled quarter can carry the load into the boot floor and spare wheel well; floor wrinkles are the sign.
sources: oem: OUTER PANELS / REAR PANEL > FLOOR / INNER PANELS (next diagram)

relations.reason: A crush hit at the rear corner can move the rear subframe; it needs measuring with parts off.
On a tailgate the rear wiper's motor sits under or through the glass; glass broken by a hit can bend its spindle.
The front exhaust pipe runs just behind and above the undercover; a dented or scraped cover often comes with a hit pipe.
The front subframe sits just above the undercover; a cover torn by a kerb, hump or debris may mean it was struck too.
The steering rack sits above the undercover; a hard strike from below can bend the rack or tie rods.
The radiator's lower edge sits above the front of the undercover; a torn front cover may mean it was hit.
A strike that pushes the undercover up can reach the lower arms at its sides; a wheel out of line is the sign.
The steering rack is bolted to the front subframe; a bent or moved subframe means the rack and tie rods need checking.
The front lower arms mount on the subframe; a bent subframe usually means the arms and alignment need checking.
The front arms bolt to the subframe; a wheel hit hard enough to bend an arm can bend or move its mount. Measure it.
The tie rods join the knuckles to the rack; a front wheel pushed back or turned usually bends a tie rod too.
The rear arms mount on the rear subframe; a bent subframe usually means the arms and alignment need checking.
On multi-link cars the rear arms mount on a subframe; a bent arm can move or bend it. Torsion-beam cars have none.
The tank sits just ahead of the rear axle; a rear wheel driven in hard can push the axle into the tank or its straps.
The rear suspension mounts on the floor and rails; a crush that moves it can wrinkle the floor above.
The engine undercover is the first thing a kerb or hump strikes under the front; scrapes underneath often tear it.
The exhaust hangs lowest under the car; scrape marks underneath usually reach the pipe, box or hangers too.
The tank sits under the rear seat area; a hard strike underneath can dent it or its straps. Fuel on the ground is the sign.
A hard strike under the rear can bend the rear subframe; it needs measuring with parts off.
The front subframe hangs lowest under the engine; a hard strike underneath often reaches it. Measure with parts off.
A hard strike under the rear can bend arms or the axle; a rear wheel out of line is the sign.
A rim dented or cracked at the lip can cut or bulge the tyre or lose its seal; check the sidewall next to the damage.
A wheel struck hard enough to dent the rim can be pushed into the arch liner and tear it.

prior.source: K2 A21: sometimes, arm, knuckle (M, H)

relations.reason: A bent or cracked rim means the blow reached the hub; arms, strut and knuckle need checking, with an alignment.

prior.source: K2 A21: sometimes, tie rod end (M, H)

relations.reason: A front wheel struck hard enough to bend the rim can bend the tie rod; a turned wheel or off-centre steering is the sign.
A tyre cut or bulged by a kerb or pothole often comes with a dented or cracked rim lip at the same spot.
A rim dented or cracked at the lip can cut or bulge the tyre or lose its seal; check the sidewall next to the damage.
A wheel struck hard enough to dent the rim can be pushed into the arch liner and tear it.

prior.source: K2 A22: sometimes, arm, axle beam (M, H)

relations.reason: A bent or cracked rim means the blow reached the hub; arms or axle need checking, with an alignment.
A tyre cut or bulged by a kerb or pothole often comes with a dented or cracked rim lip at the same spot.

chains.reason: A front pushed in far enough to bend the radiator can push it into the fan and shroud behind it.
A cover and beam pushed in at the centre, with the grille pushed in too, often reach the radiator support behind.
A bumper corner pushed back until its gaps close can drive the beam's end into the crash box and rail behind it.
A corner hit that sets the wheel back bends an arm; its mount can bend or move the subframe behind it.
A door pushed in down to its bottom edge loads the sill, which can bend the floor crossmember behind it.
A rear door pushed in down to its bottom edge loads the sill, which can bend the floor crossmember behind it.
An end panel pushed forward, with the boot floor lifted, usually wrinkles the floor and spare wheel well behind it.
A bumper pushed in until the gap to the lid closes can push the end panel and its striker forward, jamming the lock.
A bumper corner pushed in under the lamp can drive the beam's end into the crash box and rear rail behind it.
A lid whose lower edge is pushed in usually pushed the end panel too; that panel can wrinkle the boot floor behind it.
A rear corner hit that moves the wheel bends an arm or axle; on multi-link cars that can move the subframe.
A wheel set back or leaning has bent an arm; the arm's mount can bend or move the subframe behind it.
A rear wheel leaning or turned has bent an arm or axle; on multi-link cars that can move the subframe.
